reason: Considered HOLD after research (WebSearch and WebFetch were available; sources: UnitedHealth BusinessWire release-date notice, MercoPress and LBC on the Brazil first round, thriveinmarkets week-ahead calendar, Money365 10-08/10-09 closes, FXStreet and Finance Magnates on the gold correction, Wealth Professional and 247WallSt on Fed/yields). The defensive risk-premia book is +3.14% with a -2.39% max drawdown, and the EWZ take-profit at 42.98 on 10-05 banked +12.9% on exactly the event it was sized for: the 10-04 first round surprised polls (Flavio Bolsonaro ~47%, Lula ~45%) and Brazil popped. The runoff is 10-25, so re-entering EWZ now would be chasing a 13% rally into a second binary event, which is the opposite of the mean-reversion mandate; that 7% stays in cash at 4% until after 10-25. UNH (12%) reports Q3 before the open on 10-13 at 8:00 ET; the leg was entered 9-21 at 377.56 knowing the print was coming, with a deliberately wide -30% stop because the contrarian case is that the name is already deeply derated and expectations are low. Holding through the print is the consistent choice, and at 12% a +/-15% move is about +/-1.8% of NAV, inside the book's risk budget. GLD (10%, -3.5%) is ~25% below the January $5,589 record while central banks bought ~289t in Q2 (+62% y/y); the headwind is real yields with the 30-year above 5.6% and the Fed hiking, which is why this is a 10% contrarian sleeve and not a core position. TLT (5%, -4.3%) is the leg most exposed to a hot 10-14 CPI (consensus 3.6% headline, oil at $91-104), but it is small, the -8% stop sits ~3.7% below the mark and will do the exit if the term-premium thesis fails; at a 5.6% long bond the contrarian value is better, not worse, than at entry. BRK-B (+2.7%) and SVXY (+2.1%, VIX 14.8 with Fear and Greed at 70) are doing what they were bought to do. A replacement book to resize one leg would re-base every fill and stop and cost basis points for no change in thesis. Hold all legs and standing orders; revisit EWZ after the 10-25 runoff and UNH sizing after the 10-13 print.
